faq.q: What is the SSC exam photo size?
faq.a: There is none to set. SSC forms (CGL, CHSL, CPO, MTS, GD) capture a live photo with your webcam or the mySSC app instead of an upload, so no KB or pixel size applies. Use good light, a plain background, the camera at eye level, and no cap, mask or spectacles. Carry two recent passport-size colour photos to the exam.

faq.q: What is the SSC signature size?
faq.a: About 6.0 cm wide × 2.0 cm high, 10–20 KB, JPG, for CGL, CHSL, CPO, MTS and GD. At 200 DPI that is about 472×157 pixels; the GD notice asks for 300 DPI, which makes it about 709×236 pixels. The KB range is the same everywhere.

faq.q: How do I resize a signature to 6cm x 2cm for SSC?
faq.a: Open your exam above and choose the signature. SahiSize crops to the 3:1 shape, sets the pixels for 6×2 cm at the DPI your notice uses, and lands the file between 10 and 20 KB.

faq.q: Do I need an SSC photo resize?
faq.a: No. The current SSC forms capture a live photo with your webcam or the mySSC app, so there is no photo file to resize and nothing to print on it. The signature is the only image you prepare.

faq.q: Is the SSC GD signature size different from SSC CGL?
faq.a: Only in pixels (about 709×236 against 472×157, both 10–20 KB), and the SSC GD signature size page below makes the 300 DPI file.

faq.q: Can I use one signature file for every SSC exam?
faq.a: One file works for CGL, CHSL, CPO and MTS. For GD, make the 300 DPI version from the GD page.

faq.q: My SSC signature is within 10–20 KB but still rejected. Why?
faq.a: Usually because it is a "miniature" signature: small ink inside a large white image, which the notice says is rejected summarily. Crop close to the ink so it fills most of the box, and keep it dark and horizontal.

The SSC photo is captured live
You do not upload a photo for any SSC exam.

The form takes a live photo through your webcam or the mySSC app, and pointing the camera at an old printed photo gets the form rejected. Sit facing a window, camera at eye level, no cap, mask or spectacles, and retake it as often as you need before you submit.
Forms submitted with Aadhaar-based authentication are not rejected for photo or signature quality, but you still upload a signature, so make it right anyway.
